newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends stronger, market nervous.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends stronger, market nervous.

text.p: The leu closed stronger on Wednesday, when traders said the central bank intervened to support the currency, which quoted from 7,200/10 to 8,800/50 to the dollar, compared with 8,200/00 to 8,900/00 at the opening.
"The market was nervous and prices were volatile, posting wide spreads" one dealer said.
Traders said the market was starving for the leu, while demand for dollars had sagged, with some clients awaiting more attractive rates to buy currency.
They expected the central bank (BNR) to further reduce the amount on offer at its auction for one-week refinancing funds on Thursday, which would further whet "leu hunger".

Foreign exchange market operators said the BNR had intervened to prop up the leu by selling dollars. They could not say how much money the BNR had sold and the central bank declined to confirm the intervention.
"It is a good sign that the central bank finally stepped into the market after a long time," a trader said.
He said the BNR's intervention "sent a signal to the market", allowing the leu to trade at a price closer to its reference rate, currently at 7,744 lei to the dollar.
The reference rate has been stuck to the 7,744 level since Monday, when the BNR was expected to announce a new computation method for the rate. But the BNR postponed the announcement.
"Another reason behind the leu's firmer trend is commercial banks' move to increase their leu liquidity at the end of the month when payments are due," another trader said.

Latest BNR data showed interbank trading amounted to $12.97 million on Tuesday, when overall trading stood at $34.78 million. This compared with a daily average of some $609,200 in the interbank trading in January.

Leu prices at retail currency shops -- which experience the same leu shortage -- hovered at around 8,150/8,400 to the dollar, compared to 8,450/8,800 earlier in the week. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
